books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.opening: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.

books.title: Frankenstein
books.subtitle: The modern Prometheus
books.author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
books.opening: To Mrs. Saville, England. St. Petersburgh, Dec. 11th, 17—. You will rejoice to hear that no disaster has accompanied the commencement of an enterprise which you have regarded with such evil forebodings.

books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.opening: To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman. I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name. In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex. It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler.

books.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.opening: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, “and what is the use of a book,” thought Alice “without pictures or conversations?”

books.title: Dracula
books.author: Bram Stoker
books.opening: (Kept in shorthand.) 3 May. Bistritz.—Left Munich at 8:35 P. M., on 1st May, arriving at Vienna early next morning; should have arrived at 6:46, but train was an hour late. Buda-Pesth seems a wonderful place, from the glimpse which I got of it from the train and the little I could walk through the streets.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.opening: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I’ve been turning over in my mind ever since. “Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone,” he told me, “just remember that all the people in this world haven’t had the advantages that you’ve had.”

books.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.opening: The artist is the creator of beautiful things. To reveal art and conceal the artist is art’s aim. The critic is he who can translate into another manner or a new material his impression of beautiful things. The highest as the lowest form of criticism is a mode of autobiography.

books.title: Gitanjali
books.author: Rabindranath Tagore
books.opening: A few days ago I said to a distinguished Bengali doctor of medicine, “I know no German, yet if a translation of a German poet had moved me, I would go to the British Museum and find books in English that would tell me something of his life, and of the history of his thought.

books.title: The Time Machine
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.opening: The Time Traveller (for so it will be convenient to speak of him) was expounding a recondite matter to us. His grey eyes shone and twinkled, and his usually pale face was flushed and animated.

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.opening: Squire Trelawney, Dr. Livesey, and the rest of these gentlemen having asked me to write down the whole particulars about Treasure Island, from the beginning to the end, keeping nothing back but the bearings of the island, and that only because there is still treasure not yet lifted, I take up my pen in the year of…

books.title: Jane Eyre
books.subtitle: An Autobiography
books.author: Charlotte Brontë
books.opening: A preface to the first edition of “Jane Eyre” being unnecessary, I gave none: this second edition demands a few words both of acknowledgment and miscellaneous remark. My thanks are due in three quarters. To the Public, for the indulgent ear it has inclined to a plain tale with few pretensions.

books.title: Crime and Punishment
books.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
books.opening: A few words about Dostoevsky himself may help the English reader to understand his work. Dostoevsky was the son of a doctor. His parents were very hard-working and deeply religious people, but so poor that they lived with their five children in only two rooms.
